code-reviewer.why: An agent that reviews its own work tends to approve it, so a separate reviewer judges the finished change.
code-reviewer.runs: During /wettaq, after the final checks and the browser pass, for substantial changes: once to find problems, and at most once more to confirm the fixes.
code-reviewer.cannot: It cannot edit code, and it does not run the repository's full checks. It reports findings with a severity; the agent that built the change fixes them.

ui-designer.why: Interface work needs design judgement that general coding instructions do not carry, such as hierarchy, spacing and states.
ui-designer.runs: When a run, or you, hands it UI work: designing a new screen or reshaping an existing one.
ui-designer.cannot: It does not review its own work or run the repository's full checks; the main agent keeps the final verify and the independent review.
